title: Keep Things Brutally Simple
summary: Advocates prioritizing simplicity and YAGNI over premature abstractions, future-proofing, and DRY principles; argues that complexity is the primary killer of long-lived programs and that writing only necessary code today builds more reliable systems than anticipating future needs.
when-to-read: When deciding whether to add infrastructure, abstractions, or code to handle anticipated future scenarios. Distinguish from articles on code organization and modularity (see software-architecture tag), which address how to structure necessary code rather than what code should be written in the first place.
